### Summary

snapy is built on PyTorch and on three numerical packages from the same group: kintera (thermodynamics and
chemistry), pyharp (the time integrator) and pydisort (linked and imported, never called). On Linux it also depends
on commux, the communication layer of the UCX process group, and on pinc, which locates the parallel NetCDF
library. A reader who installs or changes snapy needs to know which of these are required, which versions the build
accepts, what each one is called for, and where the build metadata leaves a requirement undeclared. This appendix
lists them. The package pins of this report are the commits its citations resolve at; they are not version
constraints, and the tables keep the two apart.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** The dependency and call-site inventory of snapy's external components at the pin.

**Data.** Five packages besides PyTorch: kintera, pyharp, pydisort, commux, pinc; one version floor, kintera 2.6.13.

**Placement.** Build time (CMake locators, `pip` metadata), import time (`import snapy`) and run time (the EOS, the
saturation adjustment, the chemistry step, the stage combination, the UCX process group).

**Activation.** kintera, pyharp and pydisort are always required. commux and pinc are Linux-only: the pip metadata
requires both on every Linux install, and CMake uses them when `UCX` and `PNETCDF` are on, which is their default
off Apple.

**Guarantee / limits.** The floor is enforced for kintera alone; pyharp and pydisort are accepted at any version.

**Evidence.** @tbl-appe-checks: the pinned build of this report configures and builds against kintera 2.6.13.
:::

| component | use in snapy | required version at the snapy pin |
|---|---|---|
| kintera | moist EOS, saturation adjustment, the chemistry step | at least 2.6.13 in CMake (`find_package(Kintera 2.6.13 REQUIRED)`) and in the Python build and runtime metadata (`kintera>=2.6.13`) |
| pyharp / CMake Harp | integrator options, stage weights and stage combination | required by CMake; no version minimum |
| pydisort / CMake Disort | C++ shared-library link and Python package import | required by CMake; no version minimum |
| commux | the process group over UCX (@sec-ch14) | `commux>=0.1.4` on Linux in the Python build and runtime metadata; CMake links `commux::commux` when UCX is found |
| pinc | locates the PnetCDF headers and library (@sec-ch14) | `pinc>=0.2.0` on Linux in the Python build and runtime metadata; a `PNETCDF=ON` configure stops without it |
| PyTorch | tensors, autograd-free kernels, the process-group store | `torch==2.10.0` in the Python build metadata only; the runtime metadata declares no torch |

: Requirements, distinct from the package pins and from any tested combination. {#tbl-appe-requirements}

`find_package` declares the CMake requirements: `Torch`, `Disort` and `Harp` with no version, `Kintera 2.6.13`
({{< code CMakeLists.txt >}}). `FindKintera` enforces the floor at configure time: it reads `kintera.__version__`
and stops with "snapy requires kintera >= 2.6.13 (...)" below it ({{< code cmake/modules/FindKintera.cmake >}}); the
message names the five kintera features the floor stands for. The comment above the `find_package` line records
the steps of that floor: 2.5.8 for `SpeciesThermo` `names()`, `mu()` and `populate_thermo`; 2.5.13 for the
saturation-failure counter; 2.6.2 for the `h2o_bryan` liquid beta that `examples/bryan.yaml` needs; 2.6.3 for the
same-call rate constants of the kinetics Jacobian; 2.6.9 for the constant-$c_v$ perturbation-pressure helper;
2.6.11 for `compute_into`, which writes the moist-mixture EOS's fixed buffers. The floor itself, 2.6.13, carries
no comment of its own. The Python `[build-system] requires` and `[project] dependencies` both contain
`kintera>=2.6.13` ({{< code pyproject.toml >}}).

Neither Python list declares pyharp or pydisort, and the runtime list declares no torch. They are required all
the same, and the version a build accepts is not bounded, in four steps:

1. *The Python package imports all three.* `python/__init__.py` imports `torch`, `pydisort`, `pyharp` and `kintera`
   before it loads the compiled extension, so `import snapy` fails without any of them
   ({{< code python/__init__.py >}}).
2. *The C++ library links all three.* `src/CMakeLists.txt` lists `DISORT_LIBRARY`, `HARP_LIBRARY` and
   `KINTERA_LIBRARY` among the `PUBLIC` link libraries of the `snap` target ({{< code src/CMakeLists.txt >}}), and the
   top-level `find_package(Disort REQUIRED)` and `find_package(Harp REQUIRED)` stop the configure without them.
3. *The locators read a version but are given none to compare.* `FindHarp` and `FindDisort` run
   `import pyharp; print(pyharp.__version__)` (likewise for pydisort) once the library is found, and stop if that
   import fails. They pass the result as
   `VERSION_VAR`, but `find_package` is called without a version argument, so any found version is accepted
   ({{< code cmake/modules/FindHarp.cmake >}}, {{< code cmake/modules/FindDisort.cmake >}}).
4. *Hence* their absence from `pyproject.toml` is a packaging gap, not evidence that they are optional, and no
   compatible version range can be read from the metadata. The package pins of this report fix the API evidence;
   they are not version constraints.

### Derivation

This appendix inventories interfaces and dependencies; it introduces no numerical scheme or equation.
Thermodynamic, integration and moist-coupling derivations belong to @sec-ch02, @sec-ch09 and @sec-ch10; the
chemistry step is derived in @sec-ch10-kinetics and the saturation adjustment in @sec-ch08. A linked library, an imported Python package and a numerical call are separate facts and are
recorded separately.

### Numerical method

**kintera: thermodynamics.** Both moist equations of state own a kintera `ThermoY` module. The closed-form
`ideal-moist` EOS creates one and reads its molecular weights and reference heat capacities into buffers
({{< code src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp IdealMoistImpl::reset >}}), and calls the constant-$c_v$ perturbation-pressure helper
when it forms the anomaly pressure ({{< code src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp IdealMoistImpl::perturbations >}}); the
`moist-mixture` EOS creates one and computes
through it ({{< code src/eos/moist_mixture.cpp MoistMixtureImpl::reset >}}). The conversion from conserved to
primitive variables writes two fixed buffers in place, the inverse volumes (`DY->V`) and the temperature
(`VU->T`), then forms the pressure (`VT->P`) ({{< code src/eos/moist_mixture.cpp MoistMixtureImpl::_cons2prim >}});
the mixture heat capacity is `VT->cv` over the same volumes
({{< code src/eos/moist_mixture.cpp MoistMixtureImpl::specific_heat_cv >}}), and the primitive cache is refilled
from pressure and volume (`PV->T`) ({{< code src/eos/moist_mixture.cpp MoistMixtureImpl::_ensure_cache >}}). The
EOS reader hands the deck file to kintera, whose `ThermoOptionsImpl::from_yaml` takes its keys straight from
`dynamics/equation-of-state` (snapy's own key check lists `max-iter`, `ftol` and `uv-solver` as the keys kintera reads
there) ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}), and refills kintera's species table
before it caches the cloud parents, because a later deck can declare other species
({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::cache_cloud_parents_ >}}).

**kintera: the saturation adjustment and its counter.** The block finds its `ThermoY` by name under the EOS
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::thermo >}}) and prepares it before the first adjustment or a
capture: `prepare` gives the failure counter, the active-set buffers and the table their interior shape, device
and dtype ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::prepare_thermo overload=2 >}}; kintera `ThermoYImpl::prepare`
([`kintera thermo_y.cpp:126-135`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/0429d795f79a0665afeca565e5a05c87ab4ba1e2/src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp#L126-L135))).
When an FP32 anomaly state adjusts in FP64 totals, the state's own table is built in kintera's store first
(`tables_for`), so no call inside a capture swaps the module's table. On the final stage the block calls
`ThermoYImpl::forward` on the interior with density, internal energy density and species mass fractions, writes the
adjusted fractions back, and posts rows 1 and 2 of the failure counter (the temperature and pressure solves that
did not converge) to the monitor ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_saturation >}};
[`kintera thermo_y.cpp:225-327`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/0429d795f79a0665afeca565e5a05c87ab4ba1e2/src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp#L225-L327)).
Row 0, the adjustment failures, is the retry cause: the redo test consumes it on the device with
`consume_failures`
([`kintera thermo_y.cpp:121-124`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/0429d795f79a0665afeca565e5a05c87ab4ba1e2/src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp#L121-L124)),
with no host read ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_redo.cpp MeshBlockImpl::local_redo_flag_tensor >}}); kintera's host
read `take_saturation_adjustment_failures`
([`kintera thermo_y.cpp:329-334`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/0429d795f79a0665afeca565e5a05c87ab4ba1e2/src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp#L329-L334))
exists and snapy does not call it. A rejected step restores the active set the step started from
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_redo.cpp MeshBlockImpl::apply_redo >}}). The stage executor keys a capture on
`alloc_epoch`, kintera's host hash of the module's buffers, so a reallocation of the counter, the active set or the
table invalidates the capture ({{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::make_key >}};
[`kintera thermo.hpp:346-359`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/0429d795f79a0665afeca565e5a05c87ab4ba1e2/src/thermo/thermo.hpp#L346-L359)),
and its warm-up save list carries the counter and the active-set buffers so that a warm-up leaves no count
({{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::save_list >}}).

**kintera: the chemistry step.** The driver installs the reactions from the deck
({{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}}; {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::set_chemistry >}}), and
the block runs them as the last op of its last stage ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_chemistry >}}).
The adapter owns a kintera `Kinetics` and a `ThermoX` ({{< code src/chemistry/chemistry_source.cpp ChemistrySource::ChemistrySource >}}).
Its step refreshes the primitives after the dynamics and the adjustment, converts mass to mole fractions and to
concentrations, evaluates the rates with their rate constants, `forward_with_rate_constants`
([`kintera kinetics.hpp:192-196`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/0429d795f79a0665afeca565e5a05c87ab4ba1e2/src/kinetics/kinetics.hpp#L192-L196)),
forms the Jacobian and advances the concentrations implicitly with `evolve_implicit`
([`kintera evolve_implicit.hpp:26-27`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/0429d795f79a0665afeca565e5a05c87ab4ba1e2/src/kinetics/evolve_implicit.hpp#L26-L27)),
then adds the FP64 increment to the species rows of the stored state
({{< code src/chemistry/chemistry_source.cpp ChemistrySource::forward >}}). A dry or reaction-free deck makes the
step a no-op.

**pyharp: the integrator.** The block creates `harp::Integrator` from its `integration` options
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reset >}}). Each stage calls `pintg->forward` to combine the stage
start, the current state and the increment into the next state, for the hydro and for the scalars
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_combine >}}); the dry-source carry takes the same
combination of the density and of the scalar state, to form the mixing ratio it carries
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::carry_dry_source >}}), and
the flux register reads the stage's weights to book amounts. The weights of the three-stage `rk3` are pyharp's
([`pyharp integrator.cpp:49-60`](https://github.com/chengcli/pyharp/blob/4721715855e937c1e8b218e964c0655f46e56e29/src/integrator/integrator.cpp#L49-L60)).
This is active solver use of pyharp, independent of any radiation functionality that package may provide.

**pydisort.** Disort is in the `PUBLIC` libraries of the `snap` shared target through `DISORT_LIBRARY`
({{< code src/CMakeLists.txt >}}). `FindDisort` locates `disort_release` and reads the version by importing pydisort
({{< code cmake/modules/FindDisort.cmake >}}); Harp likewise reads `pyharp.__version__` and requires its headers and
library ({{< code cmake/modules/FindHarp.cmake >}}). No compiled source calls a Disort solver.

**commux and pinc.** A build with UCX links `commux::commux` and, with CUDA, requires commux's CUDA sidecar
library ({{< code src/CMakeLists.txt >}}); the UCX process group is commux's, constructed by snapy with the
rendezvous store ({{< code src/layout/process_group_ucx.cpp ProcessGroupContext::_init_ucx >}}). A `PNETCDF=ON`
configure imports `pinc` to find the PnetCDF headers and library and stops without it
({{< code cmake/parameters.cmake >}}).

### Code

**What to install.** For a CPU build on Linux: PyTorch 2.10.0, `kintera>=2.6.13`, pyharp, pydisort, and, for the UCX
process group and PnetCDF output, `commux>=0.1.4` and `pinc>=0.2.0`. The versions are those of the build metadata
above; for pyharp and pydisort none is declared.

```bash
python -m pip install "torch==2.10.0" "kintera>=2.6.13" pyharp pydisort "commux>=0.1.4" "pinc>=0.2.0"
```

These metadata requirements do not establish a tested compatible combination; use the preface recipe for a complete
build ([Install and run](#sec-preface-install)).

**What the build refuses, and why.** In order, at configure time:

1. *An importable package is missing.* `FindKintera`, `FindHarp` and `FindDisort` each import their Python package
   to locate its files (`kintera.__file__` and the like, with errors silenced); when that import fails the path is
   empty, the `cmake_path` calls error, `find_path` and `find_library` find nothing, and
   `find_package_handle_standard_args` stops with "Could NOT find Kintera (missing: ...)" (likewise Harp and
   Disort). The version import, and its "cannot determine PEP 440 version of ..." stop, run only after the library
   is found (`if(KINTERA_LIBRARY)`), so that message means a found library whose Python package does not import.
   The C++ library is located from the Python package.
2. *kintera is older than 2.6.13.* `FindKintera` stops with "snapy requires kintera >= 2.6.13 (...), found ...".
3. *A library or its headers is not found.* Each locator's `REQUIRED_VARS` fails the `REQUIRED` `find_package`.
4. *`UCX=ON` without commux* (UCX is on by default off Apple; `cmake/ucx.cmake` probes for the package and stops
   with a message that UCX support requires the Python package `commux` in the interpreter's environment), *`PNETCDF=ON` without pinc*, or *`CUDA=ON` with UCX
   but without commux's CUDA sidecar*: the configure stops with
   the message that names the missing package ({{< code cmake/parameters.cmake >}}, {{< code src/CMakeLists.txt >}}).

At import time, `import snapy` fails if `torch`, `pydisort`, `pyharp` or `kintera` cannot be imported
({{< code python/__init__.py >}}).

**The excerpt.** The requirements as the top-level `CMakeLists.txt` states them:

```cmake
find_package(Torch REQUIRED)
find_package(Disort REQUIRED)
find_package(Harp REQUIRED)
find_package(Kintera 2.6.13 REQUIRED)
```

The first three lines are the unversioned requirements of item 3 of the refusal list above; the last is the floor
of item 2.

: The active call sites and dependency edges at the pin. {#tbl-appe-calls}

Read the call chain as options, construction, preparation, evaluation, then failure handling. The counter has
three rows: row 0 is consumed by the redo test, once per step, so a failure counted before the step is not charged
to it; rows 1 and 2 are posted to the monitor by the adjustment and are not retry causes.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
Disort is linked and imported but never called: the compiled `src_files` glob ({{< code src/CMakeLists.txt >}})
takes no radiation directory, and no source under it calls a Disort solver. The radiating characteristic boundary
of @sec-ch11 is a characteristic outflow condition and contains no radiative transfer. No radiative time-step
limiter exists in the pinned tree; this appendix assigns no runner keys and no radiation scheme to snapy.

The missing pyharp, pydisort and runtime-torch declarations and the unversioned CMake requirements leave the
supported compatibility ranges unresolved: the metadata bounds kintera alone.
:::

- The kintera pin of this report is the floor's own release, so the citations above describe exactly the oldest
  kintera the build accepts; a newer kintera may move the cited lines.
- `take_saturation_adjustment_failures` is part of the kintera contract the floor names, and snapy at the pin does
  not call it; the device-side `consume_failures` is the one read.
- The chemistry step and the saturation adjustment are exercised only by decks with a thermo and, for the step,
  with reactions; their tests are in @sec-ch08 and @sec-ch10, not here.
